## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: look-ahead versus following time, legal versus illegal U-turns, passing left versus right, hill-parking directions and parking distances, plus continuation facts on police stops, roundabout users, turns, parked cars, parallel parking and emergencies
Confusable pairs among the defensive-driving, turning, passing and parking rules, followed by continuation facts that did not fit part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec06-R01 | anchor: A01
To test your look-ahead, pick a fixed object in front, count one-thousand-one upward until your front bumper reaches it, and if you have not got to one-thousand-twelve, look farther; at freeway speeds look at least 20 to 30 seconds ahead. [A01]
Why it matters: group space management; confusable look-ahead versus following time.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R02 | anchor: A01
To test following distance, start counting when the rear of the car ahead passes a fixed point such as a sign; reaching that point before one-thousand-two means you are too close. [A01]
Why it matters: group space management; confusable look-ahead versus following time.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R03 | anchor: A01
Keep room to maneuver by adjusting speed and lane position so you sit between the clusters of vehicles ahead and behind, in the lane that leaves you the most escape options. [A01]
Why it matters: group space management; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0042]

FACT_ID: sec06-R04 | anchor: A02
Moving violations such as speeding, running a light or sign, not signalling or leaving your marked lane are the most common reason police stop a vehicle, and drivers can break a law without knowing it. [A02]
Why it matters: group police stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R05 | anchor: A02
Officers usually ask for identification first and explain the stop second; hand over the papers promptly and without argument, and contest a citation later by requesting a court hearing rather than arguing at the roadside. [A02]
Why it matters: group police stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec06-R06 | anchor: A03
Large trucks and trailers may run their rear wheels over the raised truck apron around a roundabout's center island to manage the tight turn, but cars should stay off the apron. [A03]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; confusable truck apron versus circulating lane.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R07 | anchor: A03
Cyclists comfortable in traffic may take the lane in a roundabout, yield when entering, keep to traffic speed and hand-signal when leaving, or else walk the bike through the crosswalks. [A03]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R08 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians at a roundabout must stay in the marked crosswalks and never cross to the central island; they have the right-of-way but should still watch for cars. [A03]
Why it matters: group roundabouts; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec06-R09 | anchor: A04
After a right turn, enter the right-hand lane of the new road or the lane marked for the turn, and change lanes only after signalling once you are well clear of the intersection. [A04]
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R10 | anchor: A04
Many crashes come from drivers making turns, so watch for pedestrians and bicyclists, look once more in each direction before turning, and cancel the signal after joining traffic. [A04]
Why it matters: group turns; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec06-R11 | anchor: A05
U-turns are legal in a residential district when a traffic sign or signal protects you from approaching vehicles, but never in a business district except at an intersection or a provided opening. [A05]
Why it matters: group U-turns; confusable residential versus business district.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R12 | anchor: A05
On a divided highway a U-turn is allowed only through an opening in the center divider, never by crossing a dividing curb, strip of land or two sets of double yellow lines. [A05]
Why it matters: group U-turns; confusable opening versus divider.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R13 | anchor: A05
A U-turn is forbidden near a grade where visibility is under 500 feet in both directions, and local authorities and the state transportation department may ban U-turns at any location they control. [A05]
Why it matters: group U-turns; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0046]

FACT_ID: sec06-R14 | anchor: A06
When passing on a two-lane road, turn on the left signal 100 feet ahead in business or residential areas and 300 feet ahead elsewhere. [A06]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R15 | anchor: A06
On a multi-lane road you normally pass on the left where nothing forbids it, while passing on the right is allowed only on roads marked for two or more lanes your way and is risky because the other driver may not see you. [A06]
Why it matters: group passing; confusable passing left versus right.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R16 | anchor: A06
The slow-left-lane rule does not apply inside a city or town, when preparing for a left turn, when police direct you there, for an emergency vehicle on duty, when conditions or hazards require it, or while overtaking. [A06]
Why it matters: group passing; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec06-R17 | anchor: A07
Signs that a parked car may pull out include a lit turn signal, white backup lights, red brake lights and exhaust from the tailpipe; also watch for opening doors and people stepping out between cars. [A07]
Why it matters: group parked vehicles; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R18 | anchor: A07
If you must stop on a highway, get all four wheels well off the pavement if you can, leave room for others to pass, and use parking lights or four-way flashers in poor visibility or between sunset and sunrise. [A07]
Why it matters: group highway stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R19 | anchor: A07
With no curb, barrier, sign or marking to guide you, park parallel to the road, and in highway or freeway emergency parking areas always use four-way flashers or parking lights. [A07]
Why it matters: group highway stops; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec06-R20 | anchor: A08
For parallel parking on the right, choose a space about 5 feet longer than your car, pull up beside the car ahead of it about 2 or 3 feet away with rear bumpers lined up, then back slowly with the wheel turned fully right. [A08]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R21 | anchor: A08
Once the back of your front seat lines up with the other car's rear bumper, steer smoothly left to straighten; not straightening makes the right rear wheel hit the curb, and over-steering left can bring the right front fender into that car. [A08]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; difficulty high.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R22 | anchor: A08
Finish parallel parking about 18 inches from the curb, then shift to park in an automatic or to first gear or reverse in a manual, and set the parking brake. [A08]
Why it matters: group parallel parking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R23 | anchor: A08
Downhill tires turn toward the curb or shoulder, and uphill without a curb they also turn toward the shoulder; only uphill with a curb do the tires turn away from it. [A08]
Why it matters: group hill parking; confusable three hill cases.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec06-R24 | anchor: A09
No parking is allowed on a sidewalk, in front of a driveway, inside an intersection, next to or opposite a highway construction zone, beside an already parked vehicle, on a bridge or in a tunnel, or in a bicycle lane unless your vehicle is disabled. [A09]
Why it matters: group no-parking; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R25 | anchor: A09
Fire hydrant clearance is 15 feet for parallel parking but 20 feet for angle parking, and a crosswalk needs 20 feet while a roadside traffic signal needs 30 feet. [A09]
Why it matters: group no-parking; confusable parking distances.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R26 | anchor: A09
If your car breaks down, move to the shoulder or emergency area as soon as it is safe, turn on four-way flashers, and stay in or near the car on the side away from traffic, since walking on a freeway is dangerous and a trooper will stop to help. [A09]
Why it matters: group emergencies; difficulty medium.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec06-R27 | anchor: A09
Placard holders are asked to be mindful of accessible spaces with loading zones, which people needing lifts may require, and to use those spaces as little as possible. [A09]
Why it matters: group accessible parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A09 -> pdf-0050]
